question: Does trivial state-space compression explain why hidden fine-state phylogenetic memory is stronger in some visible-colour radiations than others?

analysis_frame.included_clades: the 21 clades already fixed as having genuine fine-to-coarse compression opportunity

primary_hypothesis.rationale: If hidden memory mainly arises because coarse coding creates more fine-state collisions, clades with larger pairwise collision gain should show stronger centered hidden-memory effects.
primary_hypothesis.test: Spearman rho with 99999 two-sided label permutations

secondary_rule: Report two-sided Spearman rho and asymptotic P values descriptively; no secondary predictor can rescue a failed primary hypothesis and no multiplicity-based winner is selected.

interpretation_rules.if_primary_failed: Conclude that the magnitude of hidden memory is not explained by the preregistered pair-collision measure of representation opportunity.

no_posthoc_rescue: do not add environmental predictors after seeing these results
do not choose a secondary structural metric as a new primary predictor after seeing its P value
do not drop clades based on effect direction or significance
do not transform the hidden-memory outcome to significance or absolute effect
do not modify frozen EL v0.3
